BEFORE YOUR FIRST LINE

It’s not about drawing perfectly.
Start by drawing often.

Gesture drawing is a quick exercise in observing and drawing.
Focus on seeing, not on finding a perfect answer.

Read the full drawing guide →
01 30 sec, 1 min, 3 min: what changes? ＋

In 30 seconds, capture the line of action and big shapes from head to toe. In 1 minute, add the tilt of the shoulders and hips and the weight-bearing foot. In 3 minutes, study overlaps and proportions. Whatever the time, begin with the whole pose before small details.

02 What should I draw first? ＋

Mark the head, then draw the spine’s flow in one line. Note the tilt of the shoulders and hips, then connect the arms and legs. Compare your drawing with the photo and notice how the feet support the body.

03 Practice with your own photos ＋

Select or drop several images in My Photos. Use people, hands, animals, or objects. Images stay in browser memory and clear on refresh; they are never uploaded to an image-processing server.
